question: Will the Dutch ban stay, yes or no?

lines.text: Israel is stripping Dutch diplomats in Ramallah of their diplomatic status.
lines.note: Israeli Foreign Ministry via Times of Israel, Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye, 27 Sep

lines.text: They have seven days to hand back their Israeli-issued papers. After that, their privileges and immunities end.
lines.note: Times of Israel, Middle East Eye

lines.text: It is Israel's answer to a Dutch ban on goods from Israeli settlements, which took effect on the twenty-second of September.
The Dutch ban covers the import, purchase and sale of settlement goods, and services that help that trade.
Foreign minister Gideon Sa'ar says the Dutch can represent their interests with the Palestinians from Palestinian Authority territory.
lines.note: Gideon Sa'ar, via Al Jazeera, 27 Sep

scene.quote: it may do so from Palestinian Authority territory

lines.text: The Dutch government says the settlements are unlawful, and the ban meets its legal obligation not to contribute to that.
lines.note: Dutch government, via Middle East Eye

scene.quote: The settlements in the Israeli-occupied territories are unlawful

lines.text: Trade between the two countries was worth 4.8 billion dollars last year.
Al Jazeera says the Netherlands takes about a third of farm exports from Israeli settlements.
So, will the Dutch ban stay, yes or no?

sources.title: Israel revoking credentials of Dutch diplomats to Ramallah after settlement ban takes effect

caption: Israel is revoking the diplomatic status of Dutch diplomats in Ramallah, days after the Netherlands banned trade in goods from Israeli settlements. They have seven days to hand back their papers. Will the Dutch ban stay, yes or no?
